_doc: REGISTER OF NAMED LOCAL DIVERGENCES from the two byte-locked oracle texts
of the Workflow tool, both reproduced byte-for-byte from claude-code
* `workflow_description.txt` -- the tool description (`t`), sent on every
request;
* `workflow_authoring_skill.txt` -- the authoring reference (`wpn()`),
served by the `workflow-authoring` bundled skill on demand.
2.1.267 split what 2.1.245 shipped as one 19,200-byte description, so each
entry now names which of the two it edits via `target`.
Why this file exists: the lock used to be a single number,
`assert_eq!(DESCRIPTION.len(), 19200)`. That number cannot tell
'we deliberately diverge here, for this reason' apart from 'the text drifted
by accident' -- both read as the same red. So the oracle file stays exactly
as the binary ships it, every intentional edit lives here with an id and a
reason, and the composed description is oracle + these, in order.
Rules the tests enforce (`description_*` in lib.rs):
* `target` selects the oracle text: "description" or "skill".
* `anchor` must occur EXACTLY ONCE in that text -- and ZERO times in the
other one, so a passage that moves between the two documents fails by
name rather than silently keeping a stale target. If an oracle refresh
moves or rewords the anchored passage, composition fails by name
instead of silently landing the insert somewhere else.
* ids are unique and `reason` is non-empty -- an unexplained divergence
is the thing this register exists to prevent.
* the composed length must equal the oracle length plus the registered
inserts, so an unregistered edit to either file still trips a length
check the way the old single number did.

divergences.reason: The oracle enumerates five EXHAUSTIVE opt-in clauses and closes with 'For any other task ... do NOT call this tool.' None of the five covers the local-app create flow, so the tool description forbids that flow's only hand-off. The nearest clause requires that the USER invoked the skill; in this flow the Host's guided contract has the MODEL self-invoke `lingxi-local-app:create-local-app` (local_apps_host.rs), and that skill then specifies the Workflow call (skills/create-local-app/SKILL.md). Verified: `grep -i 'local.app' workflow_description.txt` returns zero, so no carve-out exists, and the description is live on the mobile surface (host.rs constructs WorkflowTool::new over this text). Without this clause every create is a call the model is told not to make.
divergences.anchor: - The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.
divergences.text: - A Host-owned guided contract the user started hands off to a registered skill whose instructions specify the call. Today that is only the local-app create flow: the user asks for an app, the Host contract hands off to `lingxi-local-app:create-local-app`, and that skill names the `Workflow` call as a required step. The opt-in is the flow the user started, not the tool name.
